thread:
maria-support: Hey team, ACME-prod reported a sudden latency regression after our quant calibration swap. p95 stayed ~200-300ms but p99 jumped from ~2.3s -> ~9s starting 2026-03-12T03:00:10Z. Request id sample: req_0a1b2c. No 5xxs, all 200s. Can runtime/ML triage? cc @jon-runtime @liam-ml

jon-runtime: On it. Do we know exactly which profile rollout touched that customer? link to their org?

maria-support: Org: acme-corp (org_998). Rollout timeline: quant-profile v3 deployed to hosted-south-1 at 2026-03-12T03:01:45Z. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/ops/latency?org=org_998 (shortlink).

liam-ml: I rolled int8_v3 calibration and a small fp8 micro-optim opt in earlier today. Did we set per-route fallback to fp16? That could explain higher tail if fallback was disabled.

maria-support: Checking their model config now. snippet: ```json
{
  "model": "gptx-large",
  "quant_profile": "int8_v3",
  "fp8_micro_opt": true,
  "fallback_to_fp16": false
}
```

deploy-bot: deployment event: quant-profile-int8_v3 rollout -> hosted-south-1 @ 2026-03-12T03:01:45Z by release-eng.

jon-runtime: Thanks. Can we get KV cache hit rates and batch-size distribution for their requests? If cache churn increased, int8 kernels might take different code paths.

maria-support: KV hit% for org_998 between 02:50-03:20: avg 62% -> 48% after 03:02. p99 spike correlates to cache miss increase. No spike in QPS.

sre-oncall: If cache miss rose, more tokens go through longer attention kernels and memory copies. Also check whether quantized kernels are hitting slower fallback paths (e.g., per-head strided ops). Jon, can you dump runtime debug for a sample request id?

jon-runtime: Running quick trace: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://internal-trace/trace?req=req_0a1b2c" -o /tmp/trace.req.txt

-- attached excerpt --
2026-03-12T03:02:11Z TRACE req_0a1b2c stage=kv_lookup hit=false duration_ms=410
2026-03-12T03:02:11Z TRACE req_0a1b2c stage=attn_kernel kernel=int8_attn_v2 duration_ms=1120
2026-03-12T03:02:12Z TRACE req_0a1b2c stage=kv_store duration_ms=85
2026-03-12T03:02:12Z TRACE req_0a1b2c stage=send_tokens duration_ms=55

jon-runtime: That attn kernel line looks long. On int8_v3 we've seen a pathological path for sequences >512 when kv cache miss forces a different attention tiling.

liam-ml: Agree. Calibration changed block sizes; combined with cache-miss it triggers the slow tiling. Two immediate mitigations: 
1) enable per-route fallback_to_fp16 for ACME until we stabilize; 
2) temporarily pin them to int8_v2 which uses the old, faster tiling.

maria-support: Can we do (1) right away? How?

jon-runtime: Yes. We have a per-tenant override. Quick commmand (internal admin):
```bash
redwood-admin set-tenant-config --org org_998 --key quant.fallback --value fp16 --scope route:/api/generate
```
I'll apply and monitor.

release-eng: I can also pin them to model_variant gptx-large@int8_v2: ```bash
redwood-admin pin-variant --org org_998 --variant gptx-large@int8_v2
```
That requires a short config push but no infra restart.

maria-support: Applying fallback now.

-- 4 minutes pass --

maria-support: Update: After enabling per-route fallback_to_fp16 p99 dropped from 8.9s -> 2.9s within 90s. p95 unchanged. ACME reports user-facing latency acceptable for now. :thumbsup:

jon-runtime: Good quick win. We still need root cause. Liam, can you reproduce locally with the same prompt set and the int8_v3 profile + cold cache? If so, we should add a unit perf test.

liam-ml: Repro plan: 
1) Checkout calib/int8_v3 branch
2) Run perf harness w/ acme_prompt_set.json (I'll sync sample set to /tmp/acme_prompts)
3) Clear KV cache before each run to force misses (env RUN_WITH_EMPTY_KV=1)
4) Measure p50/p95/p99 and capture kernel traces
Command: ```bash
RUN_WITH_EMPTY_KV=1 ./perf/run.sh --model gptx-large --quant int8_v3 --prompts /tmp/acme_prompts --reps 500 --dump-traces /tmp/traces
```
I'll start this now and post results.

sre-oncall: Also check batch sizing. If their requests had slightly larger batches after the rollout (client-side change), int8 kernels might regress non-linearly. Maria, did ACME change client batching?

maria-support: ACME confirms no client code changes; they use single-turn requests. But they did ramp a new product workflow at 03:00 that increases average sequence length (more context).

liam-ml: That explains it: longer contexts + cache misses + new block tiling = p99 spike. We'll reproduce and propose mitigation: adjust calibration to prefer smaller block tiling for long-context workloads or enable fallback heuristics based on seq_len and kv_hit.

jon-runtime: For medium-term fix, two options: 
- Revise int8_v3 quant calibration to avoid that tile for >512 sequences (ML work).
- Add runtime heuristic: if seq_len > 512 AND kv_hit_rate < 60% then force fallback_to_fp16 or route to fp16 variant. This is low-risk and can be toggled per-tenant.

maria-support: Customers asks: will pinning to int8_v2 increase cost? They flagged budgeting concerns.

release-eng: int8_v2 is marginally cheaper than fp16. fp16 fallback will increase token-cost by ~12-18% for ACME's mix. Recommend we tell them about the delta and offer an incident credit for the regression window.

maria-support: I'll propose: keep fp16 fallback while we ship a targeted int8 calibration patch, propose credit for 3 hours of elevated latency window.

liam-ml: Perf run results (summary): with empty KV and int8_v3: p99 ~8.4s; with int8_v2 p99 ~2.6s; with fp16 fallback p99 ~2.1s. Kernel traces show int8_v3 taking extra memory-copy step during attention for seq_len>512. Attaching /tmp/traces summary (internal).

jon-runtime: Good data. Action items: 
- liam-ml: create PR that adjusts calibration tiling and adds unit perf test (ETA 48h).
- release-eng: roll forward pin to int8_v2 for org_998 until patch (if ACME approves) (ETA 30m to exec).
- jon-runtime: add runtime heuristic toggle behind feature flag (ETA 24h).
- maria-support: communicate with ACME, confirm credit and config change (ETA 15m).

maria-support: ACME approved pin to int8_v2 and temporary fp16 fallback for route:/api/generate. They've accepted credit offer. I'll close incident after 24h monitoring.

sre-oncall: Recommend we add a monitoring alert that correlates new quant profile rollouts with a KV hit-rate delta and p99 increase in the first 10 minutes. Catch rollout regressions earlier.

release-eng: I'll add a canary gate to future quant-profile rollouts to run perf checks for >512 seq_len cases.

maria-support: Thanks everyone — great triage. I'll file a short post-incident note and close thread when stable. :pray:

release-eng: :thumbsup:

jon-runtime: marking follow-ups in debug board.

liam-ml: starting PR now, will @mention this thread when ready.
